The full collection is available at http://www.emis.de/j
arxiv-1603-03570.creator: Valentin BONZOM
arxiv-1603-03570.description: Abstract We review an approach which aims at studying discrete (pseudo-)manifolds in dimension d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 and called random tensor models. More specifically, we insist on generalizing the two-dimensional notion of p p -angulations to higher dimensions. To do so, we consider families of triangulations built out of simplices with colored faces.

arxiv-2104-04602.title: Second quantization approach to COVID-19 epidemic
arxiv-2104-04602.creator: Leonardo Mondaini, Bernhard Meirose, Felipe Mondaini
arxiv-2104-04602.description: Abstract In this article, a stochastic SIR-type model for COVID-19 epidemic is built using the standard field theoretical language based on creation and annihilation operators. From the model, we derive the time evolution of the mean number of infectious (active cases) and deceased individuals.

arxiv-2111-12265.title: Distribution Estimation to Automate Transformation Policies for Self-Supervision Thanks: Qualcomm AI Research is an initiative of Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.
arxiv-2111-12265.creator: Seunghan Yang, Debasmit Das, Simyung Chang, Sungrack Yun, Fatih Porikli
arxiv-2111-12265.description: Abstract In recent visual self-supervision works, an imitated classification objective, called pretext task, is established by assigning labels to transformed or augmented input images. The goal of pretext can be predicting what transformations are applied to the image. However, it is observed that image transformations already present in the dataset might be less effective in learning such self-supervised representations.

arxiv-2310-05235.title: XLS-R fine-tuning on noisy word boundaries for unsupervised speech segmentation into words
arxiv-2310-05235.creator: Robin Algayres, Pablo Diego-Simon, Benoit Sagot, Emmanuel Dupoux
arxiv-2310-05235.description: Abstract Due to the absence of explicit word boundaries in the speech stream, the task of segmenting spoken sentences into word units without text supervision is particularly challenging. In this work, we leverage the most recent self-supervised speech models that have proved to quickly adapt to new tasks through fine-tuning, even in low resource conditions.

arxiv-2506-15729.title: On the transpositional relation for nonholonomic systems
arxiv-2506-15729.creator: F. Talamucci
arxiv-2506-15729.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by F. Talamucci. This paper investigates the dynamics of nonholonomic mechanical systems, with a particular focus on the fundamental variational assumptions and the role of the transpositional rule. We analyze how the C ˇ \check{\rm C} etaev condition and the first variation of constraints define compatible virtual displacements for systems subject to kinematic constraints, which can be both linear and nonlinear in generalized velocities.

pmc-10650745.title: Emodin-8-O-Glucoside—Isolation and the Screening of the Anticancer Potential against the Nervous System Tumors
pmc-10650745.creator: Estera Okon, Maryna Koval, Anna Wawruszak, Adrianna Slawinska-Brych, Katarzyna Smolinska, Myroslav Shevera, Andrzej Stepulak, Wirginia Kukula-Koch
pmc-10650745.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Emodin-8-O-glucoside (E-8-O-G) is a glycosylated derivative of emodin that exhibits numerous biological activities, including immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, hepatoprotective, or anticancer activities. However, there are no reports on the activity of E-8-O-G against cancers of the nervous system. Therefore, the aim of the study was to investigate the antiproliferative and cytotoxic effect of E-8-O-G in the SK-N-AS neuroblastoma, T98G human glioblastoma, and C6 mouse glioblastoma cancer cells. As a source of E-8-O-G the methanolic extract from the aerial parts of Reynoutria japonica Houtt.

pmc-11443782.title: Patient and professional perspectives on physical activity promotion in routine cancer care: a qualitative study
pmc-11443782.creator: Kadia Saint-Onge, Jany St-Cyr, Isabelle Doré, Lise Gauvin
pmc-11443782.description: BackgroundsPhysical activity is associated with many benefits in reducing cancer symptoms and treatments side effects. Yet, studies consistently show that knowledge about physical activity is under-promoted among people diagnosed with cancer. Therefore, we aimed to contribute to filling this gap by ascertaining patient and professional perspectives regarding physical activity promotion.MethodsThis study took place in Montreal, Canada.

pmc-11602974.title: AMH regulates a mosaic population of AMHR2-positive cells in the ovarian surface epithelium
pmc-11602974.creator: Elizabeth R. Smith, Dorcus Ye, Shihua Luo, Isaac R.L. Xu, Xiang-Xi Xu
pmc-11602974.description: The function and homeostasis of the mammalian ovary depend on complex paracrine interactions between multiple cell types. Using primary mouse tissues and isolated cells, we showed in vitro that ovarian follicles secrete factor(s) that suppresses the growth of ovarian epithelial cells in culture.

pmc-11710044.title: Analysing the Genetic Mosaic of Relapsing Remitting vs Clinically isolated syndrome Multiple Sclerosis: A Bioinformatics Perspective on Subtype‐Specific Variations
pmc-11710044.creator: Aman Milind Bhonsale, Ishita Varma, Atharva Subhedar, Shreya Khankar, Snehal Chandak, Mahima Suryawanshi, Siddhali Mast, Tapesh Lalotra, Parth Phadke, Sarthak Pakhmode, Satyendra Tripathi, Vishwajit Deshmukh, Ashlesh Patil
pmc-11710044.description: BackgroundMultiple Sclerosis (MS) is a chronic, etiologically complex disease of the central nervous system (CNS) characterized by inflammation, demyelination, and neuronal damage. MS has seven categories based on disease course. Seventy to eighty percent of individuals with MS initially develop a clinical pattern with periodic relapses and remissions, called relapsing‐remitting MS (RRMS).

pmc-11812681.title: Assessing the impact of COVID-19 pandemic on maternal healthcare usage: evidence from routine health data in Kenya and Ethiopia
pmc-11812681.creator: Michael Give Chipeta, Maame Brayie Peterson, Ruth Vellemu, Sahra Mohamed, Themba Mzembe, Chimwemwe Chifungo, Nyovani Janet Madise
pmc-11812681.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). ObjectivesLockdowns and fear of COVID-19 may have reduced access to antenatal care (ANC) and skilled birth attendance (SBA) in sub-Saharan Africa, which could undermine progress towards maternal and child survival and the sustainable development goals (SDGs).

pmc-12565070.title: DiabCompSepsAI: Integrated AI Model for Early Detection and Prediction of Postoperative Complications in Diabetic Patients—Using a Random Forest Classifier
pmc-12565070.creator: Sri Harsha Boppana, Sachin Sravan Kumar Komati, Raja Hamsa Chitturi, Ritwik Raj, C David Mintz, Giuseppe Migliaretti
pmc-12565070.description: Background/Objectives: Postoperative complications such as wound infections and sepsis are common in diabetic patients, often resulting in longer hospital stays and higher morbidity. This study hypothesizes that a Random Forest Classifier can accurately predict these complications, enabling early clinical interventions. The model utilizes ensemble learning to integrate diverse patient data and improve predictive accuracy beyond traditional risk assessments.

pmc-12639261.title: Evolutionary and structural bioinformatics identifies GPR89 as a conserved member of the LIMR protein superfamily
pmc-12639261.creator: Camila A. Quercia-Raty, Luka Robeson, Sebastian E. Brauchi
pmc-12639261.description: Also called the Golgi pH regulator (GPHR), GPR89 is an orphan membrane protein found in nearly all eukaryotic lineages. Despite its broad phylogenetic distribution, the evolutionary history, structural diversity, and function of GPR89 remain poorly understood. In this study, we present a comprehensive bioinformatic analysis of GPR89 in Eukarya by integrating phylogenetic reconstruction, genomic synteny, sequence conservation, and structural modeling.

pmc-12727553.title: Effect of the combination of acupuncture based on Yuan-Luo Da-Jie-Jing and repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation on type 1 complex regional pain after stroke: a randomized controlled trial protocol
pmc-12727553.creator: Huan Liu, Xin-yuan Zhang, Kun Hong, Juan Gao
pmc-12727553.description: BackgroundStroke is a major cause of death and disability worldwide. Approximately 12–25% of stroke survivors develop complex regional pain syndrome type I (CRPS-I) within 3–12 months. CRPS-I is characterized by severe limb pain, abnormal pain, and vasomotor instability, which hinders rehabilitation. Insufficient efficacy and adverse reactions limit the use of current pharmacological treatments, such as non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and gabapentinoids.

pmc-13035460.title: The Core Components and Instruments of the Therapeutic Relationship in Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy: A Systematic Integrative Review
pmc-13035460.creator: Sini Puustinen, Tarja Kvist, Minna Stolt
pmc-13035460.description: BackgroundThe therapeutic relationship is meaningful and valuable to patients in rehabilitation and is positively associated with improved rehabilitation outcomes. Despite its central role, a comprehensive understanding of what constitutes the therapeutic relationship in physiotherapy and how it can be assessed is yet to be achieved.

pmc-13259136.title: A Simplified Wheat Protoplast Transformation System and Guideline for Avoiding Protein Localization Artifacts
pmc-13259136.creator: Leyan Li, Shuai Zhong, Shuai Liu, Fan Zhang, Zehui Liu, Ruofei Wang, Yue Zhao, Qianwen Liu
pmc-13259136.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The transient protoplast transformation system is a vital tool for studying protein subcellular localization and phase separation in wheat. However, current protocols remain underdeveloped, and the lack of systematic vector design analysis frequently leads to localization artifacts. Here, we established a simplified wheat mesophyll protoplast transformation method featuring a shortened cycle, streamlined handling, and no variety limitations, enabling stable acquisition of high-quality confocal imaging data. Using this method, we systematically examined the effects of the fluorescent tag position (N- vs.

pmc-13321789.title: Pralatrexate is a potent pan-serotype human adenovirus inhibitor through suppression of dihydrofolate reductase
pmc-13321789.creator: Xiaowen Liang, Yong Feng, Chang Xu, Yuelin Wang, Wei Yang, Jiahua Kuang, Yanling Luo, Weihua Wu, Fangfang Chang, Lifeng Fu, Yingxia Liu, Chunmei Jiang, Liuqing Yang, Fuxiang Wang, Yang Yang
pmc-13321789.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Human adenovirus (HAdV) is one of the most infectious pathogens that can cause diseases affecting multiple organ systems, posing a significant threat to public health. Currently, there are no specific antiviral therapies available for HAdV infection. In this study, three folate antagonists aminopterin (AMT), pralatrexate (PDX), and methotrexate (MTX) with potent antiviral activity against HAdV infection have been identified through a drug repurposing screening strategy.

pmc-13520155.title: Contrasting effects of mineral, farmyard manure, and integrated fertilization on soybean productivity, seed quality, and soil biochemical properties
pmc-13520155.creator: Emrah Ramazanoglu, Vedat Beyyavas, Suat Cun, Zehra Bozdag Karakeci, Songül Akdag, Zemzem Firat, Cevher İlhan Cevheri, Erdal Sakin, Ahmet Çelik
pmc-13520155.description: Mineral and organic fertilizers differ in nutrient-release patterns and effects on soil biological processes, yet their combined influence on soybean productivity, seed composition, and soil biochemical functioning remains unclear. This study evaluated soybean and soil responses to mineral, farmyard manure (FYM), and combined fertilization over two growing seasons.
